items.title: Karnataka High Court orders land acquisition officer to pay ₹1 lakh for harassing 102-year-old man
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has directed a Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) to pay ₹1 lakh in compensation to a 102-year-old man for failing to consider his request to refer his claim for inadequate land compensation to a court [B Ramaiah v State of Karnataka] . Justice R Nataraj said the SLAO, who was in office when the petitioner gave his representation in 2022, shall pay the compensation within a month or the drawing officer shall deduct the same from the officer's salary. The Court said the officer harassed the senior citizen by not considering his request for referring the dispute against inadequate compensation to a court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 from 2005. "The respondent No.2 appears to have not taken any steps to refer the dispute. This therefore shows the apparent negligence on the part of the respondent No.2 in not complying with the statutory duty prescribed under the Land Acquisition Act and also the order passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Devanahalli," the Court said. items.title: Families of victims killed in Kochi car crash seek strict action against teen driver
items.summary: The families of three people killed in the Mini Cooper car crash near Cochin International Airport have demanded strict criminal action against the 19-year-old driver, Suhail Sajeev. Three young salespersons, Devika from Wayanad, Gopika from Palakkad, and Ijaz from Coorg in Karnataka were killed in the early hours of October 11, when a speeding Mini Cooper driven by Suhail rammed into their scooter from behind near the Cochin International Airport in Nedumbassery. The incident occurred around 1.45 am near Athani signal. Gopika’s family, from Palakkad, expressed concern that the accused might use his influence to evade accountability. At a press conference, her father said, “We believe the decision to send someone accused of such a serious crime to a borstal school was intended to sabotage the case. He said, ‘Vappa [father] will take care of it.’ We believe this reflects the influence he has.” The family also alleged that two Kerala ministers were from the accused’s area and might have used their influence. items.title: Kerala High Court deletes its adverse remarks against advocate over false affidavit attestation
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday expunged adverse remarks made by a single judge Bench of the Court against a young lawyer for allegedly allowing his client to file an affidavit containing false statements in a bank account freeze case. A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji observed that although the adverse remarks were meant to caution young lawyers about their professional duties, such remarks could permanently affect the lawyer's legal career. The Court, therefore, agreed to remove such comments from the record. " No doubt, of course, the judgement speaks with a slightly harsh stone, but we are of the view that it was not intended to be so, but only to caution the counsel so that he will be more careful in the future. With that said, it will not be proper for us to leave the portions of that judgement, which appear to speak against the council without being interfered with, for the singular reason that this will certainly have an impact on his future perpetually, " the Court said. items.title: Delhi High Court rejects SpiceJet's plea for extension of time to deposit ₹144 crore
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday refused to entertain SpiceJet's plea seeking an extension of time to deposit the money it was ordered to pay in connection with a long-running arbitration dispute with Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways. Justice Vinod Kumar also refused to accept managing director Ajay Singh's Gurgaon property as security since SpiceJet failed to deposit ₹50 crores with the Registrar General of the Court in accordance with an earlier order. "Had the petitioner [SpiceJet] deposited ₹50 crores, this Court could have entertained the plea of depositing the document of property in Gurgaon as security for permitting the amount of ₹94 crores. However, as the petitioner has not deposited ₹50 crores as per his undertaking, I am not inclined to accept the property as security. Application dismissed," the bench said. Justice Vinod Kumar In total, SpiceJet and Ajay Singh are required to deposit ₹144 crores, as per the order passed by the Court on July 13.
